To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the new concept (Educational Complementary Activities) is a useful and valid instrument to evaluate the educational activities that are not part of formal education but which are complementary, non-formal, extra-curricular or para-school.
we developed and validated a diagnostic evaluation scale for ECP activities, the EDDECP, and that we applied the EDDECP to evaluate the educational quality of science museums in Spain.
the EEDECP is a valid and reliable tool to assess the quality of ECP activities in museums.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a new concept of educational intervention (Educational Complementary Out-of-School, ECP) that is not part of the school curriculum and is aimed at students in primary, secondary and compulsory education.

the design of a new concept (Educational Complementary Out-of-School, ECP) that integrates a wide range of educational activities aimed at compulsory and adjuvant education students, and which, although not part of the curricula, in most cases using non-formal resources, pursue integral development goals under the principle of lifelong learning.

the development of a new concept (Complementary Education for Primary Education, ECP) which includes all the actions with an educational intention, directed to students of the compulsory and adjoined education and that are not included in the curriculum and didactic programs of the schools, using in most cases informal resources, and that pursue the objectives of integral development under the principle of education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this thesis has provided a new concept of education complementary to school (ECP) that has been defined and delimited in order to identify a series of non-formal educational activities that accompany the young people throughout their initial formation, and that are not included in the school curriculum or in the didactic programmes of the educational centres.

this thesis presents a new concept (Educational Activities Outside School, ECP), which includes all educational activities that are not included in the curriculum and that are aimed at students of compulsory education, with the intention of achieving an integral education under the principle of lifelong learning.
the ECP is an educational process that takes place outside the school, with the purpose of complementing and enriching the school curriculum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed an instrument to evaluate the quality of non-formal education activities for school students, which is based on a new concept (Complementary School Education, ECP) that integrates the whole set of educational activities that are not included in the curriculum, in the didactic programs of schools, but that pursue the development of integral objectives, using mostly non-formal resources.

we have developed a new concept of education (ECP: Complement Education for the school) which includes all the actions with an educational purpose, addressed to the students of compulsory and related schooling, which are not included in the curriculum or didactic programs of the schools, using mostly non-formal resources, and which aim to achieve integral development under the principle of lifelong learning.
it has provided a new definition of the concept of non-formal education and has designed a diagnostic evaluation tool for this type of educational activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of ECP (Educational Activities Outside School, in Spanish) is a new and useful way to understand a wide range of educational activities outside of formal school settings.

the ECP concept allows the identification of a wide range of educational actions that accompany the youth in their initial formation and which, being outside of the school, apparently are not subject to the proper control and supervision for the achievement of educational processes of quality.
it has allowed us to define and delimit a new concept: Complementary Education for the school-aged population (CEPS).
